name: CBS Records (UK)
founders: CBS (Columbia Broadcasting System), via acquisition of Oriole Records
ownershipStory: The American broadcaster CBS entered the UK market by acquiring the independent label Oriole Records in 1964, renaming it CBS Records in 1965. The label signed the Clash in 1977 on a major-label deal the band was later publicly conflicted about, given punk's independent, anti-corporate ethos. CBS Records was acquired by Sony in 1988 and the label was rebranded Sony Music in 1991.
hook: An American broadcaster's record arm that bought its way into Britain, and ended up signing punk's most commercially ambitious band.
blurb: CBS entered Britain in the mid-1960s by buying a small label and renaming it. Its growth into a major label matches the way the whole UK record industry was merging into fewer, bigger companies in this period. By 1977 it was big enough to sign the Clash, a deal that sat uneasily with punk's independent spirit and is one of the clearest tests of how much of punk's stand against big business could survive a band that wanted to reach a mass audience.

songsAboutLabel.title: Complete Control
songsAboutLabel.note: Written after CBS released the earlier single 'Remote Control' without the band's consent, and aimed squarely at the label and their own management for making decisions about the group's music behind their backs.
